minutes.summary: The board appointed a library trustee, a senior work-off committee member and a historical commission member, and ratified police and DPW hires. It also took a first look at a Chapter 61B first refusal and worked on policies for ballot questions, boot drives and signs.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to adopt a policy on placing questions on a local election ballot.
The board began work on a Chapter 61B first refusal at 250 Howard Street; boards want the town to exercise it at the purchase price.
The town manager outlined FY21 special town meeting amendments: added police and fire costs, new growth, lower health insurance and deferred capital.
The finance director reported FY20 fourth-quarter collections above estimate, while ambulance receipts came in below estimate.
The board appointed a library trustee, a senior work-off member and a historical commission member, and ratified police and DPW hires.

why_it_matters: If the town exercises first refusal on 250 Howard Street, it would buy the land, and the cost would reach residents through the town budget, mostly taxes, or a Town Meeting vote.
The FY21 special town meeting amendments would change the year's spending and revenue, and residents may be asked to vote on them at that meeting.
Boot drive and sign policies are still being drafted and will set which local fundraising and signs the town allows.
watch_next: Next week: the open space and conservation chairs are invited on 250 Howard Street, and the boot drive policy is due for a vote; the warrant closes September 22.
Next week: the town manager evaluation aggregate is distributed, with a vote the week after; the sign policy is discussed again.

The main differences are the ballot policy and reserve officer votes, which the official minutes do not give a tally for, and the 250 Howard Street item, where ours records no vote and the official minutes record a 4-0 vote.
